concepts.name: Core Message Transmission
concepts.description: The process of translating a strategic priority into a memorable and actionable message that guides decisions throughout an organization.

concepts.name: Concrete Decision Heuristic
concepts.description: A simple, tangible phrase that helps people make consistent decisions without requiring detailed instructions.

concepts.name: Compact Communication
concepts.description: Reducing an idea to a concise form that preserves its core meaning while increasing memorability and usability.

problems.name: Strategic priorities fail to influence behavior
problems.description: Organizations know what matters but fail to communicate priorities in a way that consistently guides day-to-day decisions.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Finding the core is not enough; it must be communicated
insights.what_it_says: Organizations often know their priorities but fail to communicate them effectively. A core idea only becomes valuable when it is understood and applied consistently by others.
insights.why_it_matters: Execution depends on shared understanding. Strategic priorities must be translated into messages that influence everyday decisions.

examples_from_source.example_name: Hoover Adams and local news coverage
examples_from_source.what_happened: Adams identified local focus as the newspaper's core priority and repeatedly communicated it to staff through memorable language and examples.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The organization aligned around a shared principle rather than relying on constant supervision.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Leaders must communicate priorities in a form that others can remember and apply independently.

decision_rules.condition: When a strategy must be executed by many people.
decision_rules.action: Convert abstract priorities into simple, repeatable messages.
decision_rules.rationale: People cannot consistently execute priorities they do not clearly understand.

patterns.description: Convert a strategic priority into a memorable communication tool.

warnings.warning: Assuming people understand priorities because leadership understands them.
warnings.prevention: Communicate priorities repeatedly in memorable forms.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When leading teams or implementing strategy.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Useful for leadership, operations, product teams, and change initiatives.

when_not_to_use: Highly technical procedures requiring detailed instructions
tradeoffs: Simple messages improve alignment but may not capture every nuance.
insights.evidence: Finding the core isn't synonymous with communicating the core.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Concrete phrases become decision-making tools
insights.what_it_says: Simple and concrete phrases help people make consistent decisions because they translate abstract priorities into practical guidance.
insights.why_it_matters: People can apply concrete instructions more easily than abstract principles.

examples_from_source.what_happened: Hoover Adams reduced the newspaper's strategy to a simple phrase that guided thousands of editorial decisions.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The phrase provided clarity across many situations without requiring detailed oversight.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Create memorable phrases that employees can use as decision filters.

decision_rules.condition: When people must make independent decisions.
decision_rules.action: Use tangible words and examples rather than abstractions.
decision_rules.rationale: Concrete ideas are easier to understand and apply.

patterns.description: Turn a strategic objective into a memorable phrase.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When teams make frequent decentralized decisions.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Works in leadership, product development, customer service, and operations.

tradeoffs: Concrete phrases improve execution but may oversimplify complex realities.
insights.evidence: "Names, names, and names" is a simple statement that is symbolic of a core truth.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Simple messages are both core and compact
insights.what_it_says: Effective simplicity requires both identifying the core idea and expressing it in a compact form.
insights.why_it_matters: Compact messages are easier to remember, communicate, and apply.

examples_from_source.what_happened: A complex editorial philosophy was compressed into three repeated words.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The message remained memorable without losing its strategic meaning.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Reduce ideas to their smallest useful form while preserving meaning.

decision_rules.rule: Compress ideas without losing the core.
decision_rules.action: Reduce unnecessary words while preserving meaning.

warnings.prevention: Ensure compactness preserves the core message.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When creating slogans, principles, priorities, or positioning statements.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Applicable to branding, leadership, teaching, and marketing.

when_not_to_use: Legal or technical documents requiring precision and detail
tradeoffs: Compactness improves memorability but can sacrifice nuance.
insights.evidence: Simple messages are core and compact.
